ui_bugs.issue: Spec asked for data-testid='assist-fab' on the bubble button. Implementation uses data-testid='assist-bubble' instead. Functionally correct — bubble exists, opens the panel, and assist-ai-sees renders inside — but the testid name diverges from the contract written into iteration_19's review_request. Recommend aligning by adding data-testid='assist-fab' as an alias OR updating the contract to assist-bubble.

issues: Cookie consent banner ('We respect your privacy') and 'XPRIZE Jury Tour' modal stack on first visit, both partially overlapping the assist-bubble in the bottom-right corner. Cookie banner z-index is higher than the assist-bubble, which means a brand-new visitor cannot reach the floating Assist until they dismiss the banner. Consider lowering the cookie banner z-index or repositioning the FAB.

critical_code_review_comments: stripe_subscriptions.py:ensure_beta_price() — correctly idempotent: searches by metadata.kind='beta_founder' before creating, then reuses any matching active monthly EUR price on that product. Verified empirically: 3 consecutive GET /api/beta/status calls returned the same price_id, proving cache works.

stripe_subscriptions.py:count_beta_filled() — counts active/trialing/past_due/incomplete subs. Note: 'incomplete' counts unstarted checkouts that never paid — this is INTENTIONALLY conservative (a half-filled checkout temporarily reserves a spot) but could cause the counter to over-report if a high volume of users abandon Stripe checkout. Stripe abandons 'incomplete' subs after 23h, so the drift is bounded.

server.py:1378 — beta_checkout reads status, then creates session. There is a TOCTOU window: two simultaneous requests when only 1 spot remains can both pass the cap check and create two sessions. The CAP enforcement therefore relies on Stripe-side seat tracking for the 100th spot, not on app-level locking. Acceptable for a 100-seat program but worth documenting.

server.py:1392 — response computes spots_remaining as status['spots_remaining'] - 1, optimistically assuming the just-created session will be paid. The true count only updates once Stripe webhook fires. UI showing N-1 immediately is a UX choice, not a bug; but it can briefly drift below the real Stripe count if many users start checkout simultaneously.

SubscribeBeta.jsx — clean implementation. window.location.origin passed to backend (no hardcoded URL), email is optional and trimmed, 410 → soft redirect to /#pricing, success/cancel toasts from URL params. No critical issues.
AISeesIndicator.jsx — null-safe (renders nothing if both company and industry empty), uses both company_industry and industry as fallbacks. Good defensive coding.
Carryover from iter18 (still applicable): consider html.escape() in daily_digest render_html; daily_digest.send_digest_now persists system_state on force=true.
